source: FHWA Proven Safety Countermeasures index, https://highways.dot.gov/safety/proven-safety-countermeasures (read via Wayback snapshot 2026-10-22); list reduced from 28 to 23 items in July 2026
note: The six Roadway Departure items are omitted because they do not apply to intersections.

render.prompt: Repaint every pedestrian crossing at this junction as a high-visibility continental (ladder) crosswalk in bright white paint, with a solid white advance stop line before each crossing.

items.name: Medians and Pedestrian Refuge Islands in Urban and Suburban Areas

render.prompt: Add a raised concrete pedestrian refuge island with kerbs and bollards in the middle of the pedestrian crossing nearest the centre of the image, splitting the crossing into two halves.
Add a continuous raised concrete sidewalk with a kerb along the road edge nearest the centre of the image.

items.name: Dedicated Left- and Right-Turn Lanes at Intersections

render.prompt: Mark a dedicated turn lane on the approach nearest the centre of the image: a solid white lane line separating it and white turn-arrow pavement markings inside the lane.
Convert this junction into a single-lane modern roundabout with a raised circular central island and splitter islands on each approach.

fields: site_control: traffic control the countermeasure is used at (FHWA PSC fact sheets); requires_user: road user class that must be in the conflict; condition: what the observed conflicts must show for the countermeasure to address them (movements and signal entry are derived from the tracks; nighttime, pavement and driveway conditions are not observable from the conflicts alone)
